Introduction

Why Are We Here?

  • The Shift: Computation-based research is transitioning toward Frictionless Reproducibility (FR).

  • The Triad: FR driven by maturity of 3 data science principles:

    • data sharing
    • code sharing
    • competitive challenges

  • The Superpower: Empirical Machine Learning (EML) uses this triad as an emergent superpower to drive AI progress.

  • The Export: These practices can be learned and adopted by any research field to instantly accelerate its rate of progress.

Overview

The Old Way vs. The New Way

The Old Way (In-Principle Sharing)

  • A scientist publishes a paper with a beautiful chart.
  • If you want to check it, you have to email them,
  • Wait weeks for the data,
  • figure out their messy code,
  • and fix a dozen errors.

The Old Way vs. The New Way

The New Way (Frictionless Reproducibility)

  • You read a paper,
  • click a link,
  • clone their GitHub repository,
  • and run their exact analysis on your laptop in 2 minutes.

The “Singularity”

When checking other people’s data work becomes effortless, scientific progress explodes at breakneck speed.

Cheap and Massive Compute Power

  • The Stalled Engine: Around 2005, individual computer chips stopped getting significantly faster year-over-year.

  • The Smartphone Boom: Because billions of people bought smartphones, tech companies built a massive global network of cloud servers to handle all that data.

  • The Result for Data Science: Today, any undergraduate student with a laptop can rent a supercomputer on the cloud for pennies to run massive datasets. Space and processing power are no longer bottlenecks.

Data Science Matures

The Core Triad:

  1. Open Data: Exposing the raw numbers, not just summaries.
  2. Open Code: Sharing the exact scripts so others can re-run the math.
  3. Common Challenges: A shared goal where everyone uses the same dataset to compete for the best accuracy scores on a public leaderboard.

Phase Transition: When all three legs of the triad meet, researchers can reproduce or modify an outside institution’s results within minutes or clicks.

What Happens If You Hide One Leg?

🛑 No Challenges

  • You get “Open Science” but no common goal.
  • Everyone works in isolated bubbles.
  • Impossible to rank which method actually works best.

🛑 No Code

  • You get competitions with secret methods (like the Netflix Prize).
  • People win, but no one learns how they won because the code is locked.

🛑 No Data

  • You get “Bring-Your-Own-Data” science (like private medical trials).
  • You cannot verify the claims because the underlying data is a black box.

Viral Science: Zero Friction

The Meme Analogy
Why do internet memes spread across the globe in a single afternoon? Because there is zero friction to share them—you just click “forward.”

  • Viral Code: When data, code, and leaderboards are completely open, scientific ideas spread through a research community exactly like viral memes.

  • The “URL or I Don’t Care” Rule: Modern data analysts reject paywalls and broken links. If a research method doesn’t have an immediate, working link, the community ignores it and moves on.

Automated Science Tracking

  • Code as Gold: In the future, public code repositories will be treated as raw material.

  • Automated Tweaking: Data scientists will write automated scripts designed to crawl through thousands of past papers, pull down their code, and automatically swap parameters to find hidden improvements.

  • The Backwater Risk: Research fields that refuse to share their data and code due to privacy or copyright fears will be left behind and forgotten by the next generation.

Internet memes spread fast because they are funny, short, and effortless to share, not because they are “true.”

🛡️ The Pragmatist View

It took me three years to write this algorithmic base. If I open-source it now, my competitors will use my code to publish five papers before I can even finish my next draft.

🌐 The Open View

Publicly archiving your code with a timestamped DOI is the absolute best way to claim ownership, establish provenance, and legally force competitors to cite you.

Final Words

Key Takeaways

  • Open science isn’t just an academic debate—it has high-stakes civic consequences.

  • Hidden code can carry direct life-or-death consequences in engineering and public policy.

  • Perfectionism and Absolute Secrecy both break scientific progress.

Key Takeaways

In the real world, engineering projects navigate this standoff through compromised structures:

  • The Production Sandbox: Tech firms can deposit source code into a Software Escrow—allowing a trusted, independent third-party academic panel to run line-by-line audits without exposing trade secrets to public competitors.

  • The Barnes Reality Check: Code does not need to be a beautifully polished product to be verified; it just needs to expose the raw mathematical parameters governing the bridge’s stress metrics.

  • The Baseline Rule: Un-auditable code is un-verifiable science.

The Selfish Benefits of Open Code

  • Your Most Important Collaborator: Your “past self” is your most frequent collaborator, and they notoriously forget what their own code did after 6 months.

  • The “Push-Button” Advantage: Forcing yourself to build a script that replicates your whole project with the push of a button pays off massively down the road.

  • Frictionless Revisions: When a journal reviewer inevitably demands you replot your data or shift an axis, an automated script saves you weeks of manual reconstruction labor.

  • The Institutional Shield: If your results are ever publicly questioned or audited by outsiders, a public, timestamped git repository provides immediate, undeniable proof of your data’s provenance.
